items.q: we coudl play cards with Pete, Albert and some of the Gates when we had our rest periods

ctx.x: crowded that there were tables on the dance floor and there was just enough space to push the two baby grand pianos against the bandstand for Pete Johnson, Albert Ammons and Hazel Scott. For the second show at two o'clock, there were less people but still a good crowd and the show could be put on in the middle of the dance floor. The Golden Gates had to squeeze in between the two pianos when they went on for the first show.

We didn't do too much drinking at the bar because we had spacious rooms upstairs where we coudl play cards with Pete, Albert and some of the Gates when we had our rest periods, and we formed a club composed of those that liked a few tastes every night and bought our bottles of Kick-a-poo joy juice at a whisky store near the club. But if a friend came in or a client who admired a cert_ain musician invi_ted one of us at the bar, we accepted.

After a couple of weeks ef everything going well, Barney began to be Mr. Josephson because of the success of the Uptown Cafe Society. He put up a sign in our dressing room which specified that no sideman in the orchestras would be allowed to sit at a table with a client. The only exceptions were for Hazel who was the star of the show, Teddy, Eddie South, and of course, the comedian.
